idiom_name: Vapor versioned route groups + Codable DTOs (or swift-openapi-generator server stubs)
implementation_notes: Vapor publishes the protocol through route registration: app.grouped("v1").post("orders") { req in ... } is the host service, and the Codable struct you decode/return is the wire contract, so the translation layer is that DTO and the domain types stay untouched by Codable conformance. For contract-first teams, swift-openapi-generator turns a checked-in OpenAPI document into the server types and protocol you implement, which makes the document the published language and removes drift by construction. Either way, the document or the Codable DTOs are the artifact consumers bind to - the Swift types themselves are not readable by non-Swift consumers.
pitfalls: Adding Codable conformance to a domain model for persistence reasons silently publishes its fields on the wire; keep conformance on DTOs.
Async route handlers must not block the event loop with synchronous database or file work.
Without a checked-in OpenAPI document the Swift types are the only contract description, which partners on other stacks cannot consume.
